page.layout: One printed page: main text in a single column on the left, with marginal notes in a narrow column on the right. Running head at top, page number at top right, catchword and signature at the foot. The left edge of the scan shows part of the neighbouring page, which is not transcribed.

main_text.p: (inquit {g}Athanasius) de Constante loquens, martyrium assequutus est ille contra, (Magnentium intelligit), iam inde quasi in nexu esset, ad similitudinem Cain, cum gemitu et trepidatione fugiebat, vt Iudam postea eodem mortis genere imitaretur, sibique ipsi carnifex factus, duplex supplicium, & hic, & in iudicio futuro irrogauit.Apolog. ad Constantium.

Mortuis vtrisque Fratribus, vniuer-sa rerum summa Constantio cessit, vnde arrogantior esse caepit (inquit {h}Zozimus) quod eam fortunæ prosperitatem moderatè ferre non potuit; immunemque se deinde fore ab omni mortalitatis incommodo fidenter existimans (inquit {i}Ammianus) confestim à iustitia declinauit ita intemperanter: ut æternitatem meam aliquoties ipse propria manu subscriberet, suumque Cæsarem æternum appellauerunt, qui filium Dei ęternum esse negant, inquit Athanasius. Imò ipse Imperator post victoriam de Magnentio partam, Arrianissimus factus, {k}eousque Catholicos persequutus est, ut violentia non minor ea esset, quàm illi olim adhibuerant, qui ChristianosLib.3.[?]Lib.15.Soc. lib.2. cap.22.[?]

page.notes: Marginal notes read from the right margin: g "Apolog. ad Constantium."; h "Lib.3." (the numeral is hard to read, marked [?]); i "Lib.15."; k "Soc. lib.2. cap.22." (the abbreviation "Soc" is uncertain, marked [?]). The line ending "Christianos" is the last full line before the catchword. The left edge of the scan shows part of the neighbouring page and was left out.
